item.title: NYSE bets on all-or-nothing options as event driven trading gains traction
item.description: NYSE is preparing to launch binary return options that will let investors make all-or-nothing bets on whether stocks and ETFs finish above or below set prices. The exchange is also seeking approval for KPI options linked to company earnings metrics, expanding the range of event-driven trading products available to investors.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: The New York Stock Exchange is preparing to launch a new type of options contract that will let investors make all or nothing bets on whether a stock or exchange traded fund finishes above or below a specified price, as demand grows for more targeted ways to trade market events.The binary return options are expected to begin trading within days, with 12 underlying securities initially, including Apple, Nvidia, Tesla and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust. More securities are expected to be added over time.NYSE targets demand for event based tradesThe move comes as options trading and event based contracts have expanded rapidly, encouraging exchanges to develop products aimed at investors seeking more precise ways to express views on individual stocks or broader markets. We've seen this incredible growth in the US options market over the last several years. When we look inside that volume growth, there's a lot of interest in newer ways to trade or newer products to trade, Kevin Tyrrell, chief product officer at NYSE, told Reuters.Unlike traditional options, the new contracts are designed around a simple outcome. They would pay $1 or nothing at expiration depending on whether the underlying security finishes above or below the contract's strike level.NYSE also seeks approval for earnings linked optionsNYSE is also awaiting approval from the US Securities and Exchange Commission for another product that would allow investors to trade directly on company performance metrics.The binary KPI options would pay investors based on whether a company reports a specified result above or below a set threshold. The contracts could cover metrics including net sales, earnings per share, cloud computing revenue and vehicle production.The cash settled, European style contracts could only be exercised at expiration, with investors receiving either $1 or nothing depending on the reported result.Cboe Global Markets recently received approval for similar KPI based contracts in partnership with Robinhood, highlighting the wider push by exchanges to capture demand for event driven trading, Reuters reported. (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Boeing cuts delivery target, shares hit 18-month low as recovery takes longer
item.description: Boeing has announced a cut in its 737 Max delivery target for this year, which raises concerns. The company now aims to increase 737 production to 52 jets per month in the second half of next year. Boeing reported a wider than expected loss in its commercial airplane division but posted positive free cash flow results. Despite delays, the company plans to begin deliveries of its 777-9 jets next year.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Boeing shares tumbled to an 18 month low on Tuesday after the planemaker cut its full year delivery target and pushed back plans to increase production of its 737 Max jets, raising fresh concerns over the pace of its recovery, Bloomberg reported.The stock fell as much as 10%, its biggest intraday drop since April 2025, after Boeing said it would fall short of its target to deliver 500 737 Max jets this year. The company also expects deliveries of its 787 Dreamliner to come in near the lower end of its guidance.Production ramp up faces fresh delayBoeing now plans to increase 737 production to 52 jets a month in the second half of next year, up from 47 currently. That milestone had previously been targeted for the end of 2026.“As I’ve said many times before, it’s more important that we do this ramp right than what particular month we achieve a rate break, and we’ll stay disciplined here,” Chief Executive Officer Kelly Ortberg said on a call with analysts.The slower ramp up adds pressure to Boeing's efforts to strengthen cash flow after years of production disruptions, quality issues and supply constraints. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst George Ferguson said the reaction reflected the importance of higher commercial aircraft production to Boeing's finances.“I think he’s being honest, but I think what that does is push all the cash flow expectations to the right,” Ferguson said.Boeing's commercial airplane division posted a $697 million third quarter loss, wider than the $360.8 million deficit expected by analysts surveyed by Bloomberg. The division's loss was nevertheless substantially lower than a year earlier.Cash flow offers some reliefFree cash flow provided a brighter spot, reaching $464 million in the quarter and beating estimates of $325.1 million. Boeing expects to generate about $2 billion in free cash this year, $3 billion next year and $10 billion by 2029.The company also reiterated that it plans to begin deliveries of its 777-9 next year, although the programme is running about six years behind schedule.Ortberg said Boeing has significantly reduced risks across its portfolio, while the company continues to deal with engine and supply chain constraints affecting its aircraft production. item.title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as premium drinks, sodas hold strong
item.description: Coca-Cola has lifted its annual profit forecast, driven by robust demand for a range of beverages, particularly zero-sugar options. The company now anticipates earnings per share growth of at least 9% by 2026. Their third-quarter revenue soared to $13.38 billion, exceeding analysts' expectations, while Coca-Cola's strong showing stands in sharp contrast to PepsiCo's recent downgrades and cost-cutting plans. Following these promising results, Coca-Cola shares rose nearly 1% in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its annual profit forecast, betting on resilient demand for its zero-sugar sodas and pricier beverages such as fairlife milk and sparkling soft drinks.The company now expects comparable currency-neutral earnings per share to grow at least 9% in 2026, up from its previous forecast of 7% to 8%.Coca-Cola's third-quarter revenue rose 7.4% to $13.38 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $12.92 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.As high food and fuel prices make consumers more selective, Coca-Cola has sought to sustain demand by offering smaller, cheaper packs while rolling out pricier new flavours such as Coca-Cola Cherry Float.The company also benefited from demand during the soccer World Cup in July, including a brief sales boost for its energy drink brands.Its performance contrasts with rival PepsiCo, which lowered its annual targets earlier this month and stepped up cost cuts as it grapples with weak demand for snacks in North America.Coca-Cola shares rose nearly 1% in premarket trading. The stock has jumped about 33% in 2026 and is on track for a third straight year of gains, despite broader weakness in consumer spending and market volatility stemming from the war in Iran.
